provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

provisions.text: APIs tend to expose endpoints that return all object’s properties. This is particularly valid for REST APIs.

provisions.title: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
provisions.text: The product generates a hash for a password, but it uses a scheme that does not provide a sufficient level of computational effort that would make password cracking attacks infeasible or expensive.

provisions.title: Active Debug Code

examples.label: positive
negative

value.reason: The public route GET /rest/memories (server.ts:670) has no authorization middleware. It calls MemoryModel.findAll({ include: [UserModel] }) (routes/memory.ts:24) with no `attributes` allowlist or exclusion on the included UserModel, so each memory record comes back with its full nested User record. The User model defines sensitive properties: the password hash (stored with security.hash, a weak scheme), a redacted secret-type field (models/user.ts:97-100 and 109-112), lastLoginIp, email and username. The excerpt doesn't show the line that sends the response, but this is a retrieval endpoint and the pattern matches the positive example. Unauthenticated users can therefore read every user's object properties, which is broken object property level authorization and a failure to apply reasonable access-control safeguards to personal data.
